note: PRE-07 still open. Habitat uses cited Sol 4527 waypoint; boxwork bonus uses cited Sol 4534 waypoint. The two lake-sediment stops are real Curiosity drill sites in the Glen Torridon clay-bearing unit (Glen Etive 1, Mary Anning 3), at the rover's parked waypoint. All four sit inside DTEEC_009149 (the streamed corridor terrain). All is_example true until the team locks the stops.

properties.science_summary: Illustrative EVA start at the cited Curiosity Sol 4527 waypoint (near boxwork entry). Not a human landing-site claim. Gale is a rover site. PRE-07 not locked.
properties.source: MSL waypoints Sol 4527 (cited candidate; not locked)

properties.name: Glen Etive 1 drill site (Glen Torridon, Sol 2486)
properties.science_summary: Curiosity drilled Glen Etive 1 on Sol 2486 in Glen Torridon, the clay-bearing unit with the highest clay abundances of the mission. Bennett et al. (2023) read the lowest Glen Torridon strata as a continuation of the lacustrine Murray formation. Position is the rover's parked waypoint (Sol 2481).
properties.source: NASA Curiosity blog Sols 2485-2487; MSL waypoints Sol 2481; Bennett et al. 2023

properties.name: Mary Anning 3 drill site (Glen Torridon, ~Sol 2870)
properties.science_summary: Curiosity drilled Mary Anning 3 (go-for-drill post, Sols 2870-2871) for a SAM wet-chemistry experiment. SAM found sulfur-bearing organic molecules in Glen Torridon samples; Millan et al. (2022) suggest clay minerals helped preserve ancient organic matter. Position is the rover's parked waypoint (Sol 2829).
properties.source: NASA Curiosity blog Sols 2870-2871; MSL waypoints Sol 2829; Millan et al. 2022

properties.name: Boxwork bonus (example — Sol 4534 candidate)
properties.science_summary: Bonus stop candidate at the cited Curiosity Sol 4534 boxwork-entry waypoint (Altadena member context). Primary goal remains lake sediments / habitability. PRE-07 not locked.
